strong_form: No theoretical proposal for new fundamental particle-physics content (a new field, symmetry, or mechanism beyond what was in place by roughly the mid-1980s) has since been confirmed by experiment; the Standard Model confirmations of the last ~40 years (W/Z, top quark, Higgs, tau neutrino) all test predictions made earlier.
weak_form: Since the 1970s-80s, beyond-Standard-Model theory (GUTs, supersymmetry, technicolor, extra dimensions, etc.) has produced many predictions and no confirmations.
refuted_if: A theory-originated prediction of a new fundamental ingredient, first proposed after ~1985, that experiment then confirmed (e.g., a discovered superpartner, observed proton decay, or a new boson predicted after 1985).
synonyms: crisis in the foundations of physics

strongest_criticism: How the claim reads depends on what counts as an 'improvement': the 2012 Higgs discovery and the 1995 top quark were theory-driven predictions that nature validated within the window, even though the theory itself is older. Neutrino mass is a real change to the minimal Standard Model, though experiment drove it. Theorists made real advances in calculation (precision QCD, lattice, amplitudes) that experiment confirms, so 'no theory advance' holds only for new fundamental content. On that reading the claim is well supported, but it is a widely aired critique (Smolin, Woit, Hossenfelder, Turok), not a rare insight.
